claims.text: ModuleBoundaryTests catch two changes the compiler accepts: Catalog referencing DonHang.Domain/Infrastructure/Api, and one more Catalog type made public (CatalogMakesPublicOnlyItsContract compares with CatalogModule, CatalogProduct, ICatalog).

The same test class keeps Notifications and Payments from referencing any Đơn Hàng project but DonHang.Messaging (ServiceUsesNoDonHangProjectButMessaging): a reference would load another part's code into the service's own process, which the network does not stop.

Ordering reaches Catalog with an in-process method call: OrderService asks IProductPrices for each item's current price while an order is placed; CatalogProductPrices answers through ICatalog.FindAsync.

Notifications runs in a process of its own and knows an order only from OrderMessage: order id, customer email, customer name, time; it keeps its own copy of the record, the JSON being the contract; product names are not in it.
Messages from DonHang.Api reach Notifications through RabbitMQ and wait in its queue while it is down.

claims.text: ADR 0002 counts, for Notifications: one more image, build pipeline, database and dashboard to run; calls over the network can fail; order and email are no longer saved in one transaction, the email arrives after a while.

Each step toward services buys independence in releasing, scaling and failing (a service can be built, released, scaled and stopped on its own) and pays for it with failing calls, data that agrees only after a while, and more to run.
Stage-3 Đơn Hàng mixes styles on purpose: Ordering and Catalog are modules of DonHang.Api, Notifications and Payments are services, each placed by its own drivers.

Trade-offs table: who holds the boundary (people / compiler and tests before merge / network while running), what a call across it is, whether parts release, scale and fail together, and what each adds to run (images, a database, build and monitoring per service).

If code tangles across modules but no driver asks for separate release or failure, a modular monolith fixes it at lower cost than a service; a Catalog service would put another process that can be down or slow inside order taking; a one-developer tool fits one process without modules.
A boundary checked at build time is a real boundary; a modular monolith is a style with its own place, not a step before services; mixing modules and services is not a half-finished migration.

order_items (product id, quantity, price; no name) is in the donhang database owned by Ordering, on the same PostgreSQL server, user and password as donhang_notifications; no tool stops Notifications opening a second connection to donhang.
